arms.predicted: Grid NN construction with time-guarded 2-opt will score significantly above the x-sorted baseline (score >> 0), achieving score >= 78 on the judge. The dominant factor is construction quality (visiting nearby cities via spatial grid), not penalty optimization.
arms.observed: Score: 78.428 (stable across 4 runs: 78.428, 78.428, 78.428, 78.4275). The grid NN construction with candidate-list 2-opt using fast penalty-aware delta (O(1) Euclidean + O(seg/10) penalty) consistently achieves ~78.4. The penalty (carrot constraint) is confirmed as a ~1% effect — pure Euclidean NN scores 78.19, and penalty-aware 2-opt adds ~0.2 points. SA and ILS variants were tested but proved unstable (73-78 range) due to timing sensitivity. The deterministic greedy approach dominates.

metadata.approach: Grid NN (G=sqrt(N/4)) + candidate-list 2-opt (K=5-10 spatial neighbors, seg_limit 200-500) with fast penalty delta

discrepancy_analysis: Prediction confirmed: score >= 78 achieved consistently at 78.43. The dominant factor is construction quality (grid NN), not penalty optimization. The fast 2-opt delta computation (O(1) Euclidean + O(seg/10) penalty positions) enables candidate-list 2-opt for all N sizes, adding ~0.2 points over pure NN. Advanced local search (SA, ILS) provides marginal and unstable improvements, confirming that the NN construction quality is the bottleneck.
